options.text: The Blade is Metal in its yang form, the ore that went into the forge soft and came out with an edge. Its season is autumn, when the year stops growing things and starts choosing which of them to keep. Steel like this does one job. It cuts, once, and the cut stays cut. Left alone it wants nothing, asks nothing, and rusts only where it was never used. A sword hung over a doorway keeps the whole house honest without saying a word.

The Blade is Yang Metal, the metal that has already been through fire. It arrives with autumn, the season that ends what summer started, and it does the harvest's honest arithmetic, deciding what was worth growing. Kept plain and kept sharp, it is drawn once, only for the true thing. Between wars it hangs on the wall and says nothing, which is its own kind of speech.

options.text: You are what the sword is like when it wakes up as a person. You put the truth ahead of comfort, yours and everyone's, every day. The straight answer is out of you before anyone asked for it. You say it because it is true, or you say it because softening it would feel like lying. You are left with the truth and a little less company each time, the price of being right.

You are what the sword is like when it wakes up as a person. The cut is always ready and mostly used. You put the truth ahead of comfort, yours and everyone's, every day, in every setting. People bring you the questions nobody else will answer straight, then flinch at exactly what they asked for. The edge never rests. That includes the nights, and it includes you.

The mountain holds the ore for ages before any edge is struck from it, and every blade remembers the patience of the rock that made it.

options.text: The hard prevails over the soft, the classics say, and so metal governs wood. The axe meets the trunk, the knife meets the branch, and the wild green yields shape it could not find alone. The cut is craft rather than ruin: forest becomes timber, bramble becomes orchard, under an edge that knows what to spare.

The knife exists for the branch. Wood grows in every direction it can reach, and left alone it grows into a thicket that shades its own fruit. So the old texts set metal against it, hard against soft, the cut that gives a living thing its shape. The pruned tree bears more than the wild one. Steel and timber are not enemies. One is what the other is for.

options.text: word: Won't bend  |  text: Your own standard is the only one you answer to. You hold it because it is right, or you hold it because bending would feel like losing yourself. The price is company that can match you, which is rare.

word: Sealed-off  |  text: Letting people in stopped being something you decline and became something you cannot quite locate. Fine, you say, on the day of the diagnosis, the layoff, the breakup. The word has three hundred uses now, and not one of them means fine.

word: Unreadable  |  text: You keep your own counsel, and it passes for freedom. Metal is heavy in you, so the surface holds. options.text: Water is what metal becomes when it stops holding its shape. In the old texts the cold blade gathers dew out of the morning air, and metal melted in enough heat runs like a river. So the child of steel is the stream. What the edge kept hard and silent, the water carries off and says. A spring under a mountain is the ore learning to move.

In the old reckoning water is metal's child: cold iron beads the morning dew, and metal, melted, runs bright as any river. The hard thing does not stay hard. At its finest edge it turns liquid, and what was fixed begins to flow, the clear stream carrying the mountain's sharpness out into the world.

word: Decisive  |  text: Deciding fast is native wiring for you, and it reads as relief to everyone stuck deliberating. Options do not improve with age, in your experience, and your experience keeps proving it. The choice gets made while others are still framing the question. Then everyone breathes.

word: Takes charge  |  text: You take charge the moment nobody else does, and sometimes a moment before. You have little Fire, and what there is gets spent at the front. You step in because it needs doing, or because waiting means you get passed over. The price is that nobody ever gets the chance to ask you first.

label: Fire page (your Order, catalyst, thin) · ledger[1] (cost self, The General (七杀)) · ELEMENT_GOD.fn_reading

options.text: word: Runs toward it  |  text: Trouble is where you feel most like yourself. There is little Fire in you, so what steadies you only arrives when something breaks. You run toward the crisis because it needs you, or because calm has nothing you know how to hold. The cost is a body that only rests after a fight.

word: Daring  |  text: The call everyone dreaded sat on your list for exactly one day. You made it standing up, between two other tasks, and it went the way these things usually go with you, which is fine. Three weeks of collective dread died in four unremarkable minutes.

label: Fire page (your Order, catalyst, thin) · ledger[2] (cost others, The General (七杀)) · ELEMENT_GOD.fn_reading

options.text: word: Crisis-ready  |  text: There is a particular quiet that falls when things break and you are present, because everyone knows where the decisions will come from. It looks like glamour from a distance and it is really planning under pressure, done fast, and it has saved more days than anyone has counted.

word: Pushes hard  |  text: You push people the way you push yourself. You carry little Fire, so all of it goes to whoever is closest to the job. You set the pace because it must get done, or because slowing would mean you hand it over. The people near you pay with their own pace and never find it.

label: Fire page (your Order, catalyst, thin) · function.advise_catalyst · ELEMENT_PAIR.function.advise_catalyst

options.text: Order you have never been tested on is a guess about yourself. Sign up for one thing a year with a judge in it, a race, an exam, a review by someone senior. Take the deadline you are not sure you can make. Let one person tell you, to your face, what you got wrong this month.

Fire that only knows battle starts inventing battles. Save your command for what deserves it: decide the small stuff instantly and cheaply. Build one boring routine that runs when nothing is burning. Peacetime is what the fighting was for, so practice standing in it.

label: Fire page (your Order, catalyst, thin) · cta_verdict · ELEMENT_PAIR.cta_verdict

options.text: Rules only hold you when there is heat in them, so you do your best work under a deadline but your worst under a plan with no date on it.
Pressure is what puts you in order, so you are at your best when something is being asked of you but at your worst when nothing is.
Pressure is your forge, and the heat you choose on purpose finishes an edge that comfort would have left dull.
